title: Year four close: the ways
hook: practice and thought, law and heart, all pointing one direction

segments.voice: Yesterday, humility after learning, and your line: someone knows more. Did you say I don't know out loud, when it was true? Today, the last day of year four. Day one thousand four hundred twenty-six.

A small arrow is stuck to the ceiling of a hotel room, pointing past the wall, past the parking lot, past everything. A traveler unrolls a mat beneath it. Across town, a family lays out mats in a living room, lined up with a compass on a phone. In a mosque, the whole building is already turned that way. Different rooms, different reasons for being there. One direction. This year walked many ways into the faith: practice and thought, law and heart. Today, on its last day, we look at where they all point.
screen: `AN ARROW ON A HOTEL CEILING.` → `DIFFERENT ROOMS, ONE DIRECTION.` → `WHERE THE WAYS POINT.`

segments.voice: First, the ways this year took. Practice: the pillars, from the inside. Thought: the creed, and the reports with their careful chains. Law: the schools, standing in one row. Heart: its stations and its diseases, and the manners that show it. Then the life cycle, from the call to prayer in a newborn's ear to the last prayer, and a living ummah across the world. Second, the direction. The Qur'an tells the Prophet, in Pickthall's translation: "So turn thy face toward the Inviolable Place of Worship." That is the qiblah, the Kaaba in Mecca. Every school, every land, every hotel room, one direction in prayer. Third, the direction is not the whole of it. The same surah says: "It is not righteousness that ye turn your faces to the East and the West." Then it says, in paraphrase, what righteousness is: believing in Allah and the Last Day, giving wealth out of love to family, orphans, the needy and the traveler, keeping the prayer, keeping promises, and patience in hard times. One verse, and inside it, creed, charity, prayer, manners and heart. Law and heart in a single breath. Fourth, Who the direction is for. Earlier in the same surah: "Unto Allah belong the East and the West, and whithersoever ye turn, there is Allah's Countenance." Muslims face the Kaaba because they were told to, and worship Allah, Who is not held by any building. So the ways of this year are not rival roads. Practice and thought, law and heart, are many paths through one life, and in prayer they all turn the same way. Tomorrow, year five: the sources themselves.
screen: `PRACTICE, THOUGHT, LAW, HEART.` · `TURN THY FACE: THE QIBLAH.` · `NOT ONLY EAST OR WEST: RIGHTEOUSNESS.` · `WHEREVER YOU TURN, ALLAH'S COUNTENANCE.`

segments.voice: The practice: pray two units of thanks. If you pray, you can, after this lesson, pray two voluntary units, two rak'ahs, with the intention of thanks for the year. For now, settle into the sit. If you know the direction, turn toward it. If not, simply sit where you are. Breathe. Let one thing from this year come forward that you are grateful to have met: a verse, a person, a habit that stuck. Hold it. Let the rest of the year sit quietly behind it. The bell holds the time.

Year four close. The pillars, the reports, the schools, the creed, the heart, the manners, the life cycle, the world, and the gathering of it all: one faith, walked many ways, facing one direction. Today's word.

Your line: all roads face the qiblah. Today, the next time you turn toward something that matters, notice what you're turning from, and what you're turning to. Tomorrow, the last range. Day one thousand four hundred twenty-six.

howItsDone: Muslims face the qiblah, toward the Kaaba in Mecca, for every prayer, finding it by the mosque's prayer niche, a compass or an app; some also pray voluntary rak'ahs, or bow in a prostration of thanks, when something good happens.

myth: facing the Kaaba means praying to a building
Muslims face it because they were told to, and worship Allah; "whithersoever ye turn, there is Allah's Countenance."
the Qur'an says righteousness is not only turning east or west
2:177 then names belief, giving, prayer, keeping promises and patience.
each school of law prays toward a different direction
every school, every land, one qiblah.

fork.setup: you're in a hotel room with no arrow and no signal. you want to pray. what do you do?
options: skip the prayer until you find the exact direction.
make your best effort at the direction and pray.
face any wall without a thought.
fork.reveal: jurists teach that an honest effort to find the qiblah is enough, and the Qur'an says: whithersoever ye turn, there is Allah's Countenance.

original.note: Arabic: the direction faced in prayer, toward the Kaaba in Mecca.

trapdoor: what you thought: the qiblah is just a compass direction.
what it means: one direction for every Muslim's prayer, and a picture of many ways of faith facing the same way.
what a scholar hears: 2:144, turn thy face; 2:177, righteousness is not merely east or west; 2:115, whithersoever ye turn, Allah's Countenance.
